summary: Tri-Cities Regional TN/VA Airport serves the northeast Tennessee and southwest Virginia region, collectively known as the Tri-Cities area comprising Bristol, Kingsport, and Johnson City. The airport has roots in World War II, when the site operated as a military training facility before transitioning to civilian use. It remains a vital regional link for the Appalachian Highlands, connecting residents and visitors to major airline hubs.
faqs:
Q: Which cities does TRI primarily serve?
A: The airport serves the Tri-Cities region, including Johnson City and Kingsport in Tennessee and Bristol on the Tennessee-Virginia border.

Q: What airlines operate at Tri-Cities Regional Airport?
A: Delta Air Lines and American Airlines (via American Eagle) provide scheduled passenger service with connections to Atlanta, Charlotte, and other hubs.

Q: How large is the airport terminal?
A: TRI has a single, compact passenger terminal that allows travelers to move quickly from curb to gate, typically in just a few minutes.

Q: Is the airport open 24 hours?
A: The terminal operating hours vary by flight schedule, but the airfield itself accommodates general aviation around the clock.
transport_tips: The airport sits near the junction of I-81 and I-26, making it accessible from any of the Tri-Cities within roughly a 20-30 minute drive. On-site rental car agencies and taxis serve the terminal, and rideshare pickup is available in the designated lot. Ample free parking, including short- and long-term lots, is available directly adjacent to the terminal building.
local_tip: If you have a layover or extra time, the Bristol Motor Speedway and the historic Bristol Sign—spanning State Street across the Tennessee-Virginia line—are within about 15 miles of the airport and offer a uniquely local experience.
